answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The canyon multiplier is published, charged in river, and kernel lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1167 identities would post 2373 proofs and burn roughly 62 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
